newsitem.title: USA: Shut Santa Fe Phoenix line to restart Thurs.
newsitem.headline: Shut Santa Fe Phoenix line to restart Thurs.

text.p: A section of Santa Fe Pacific Pipeline will reopen late Thursday after a precautionary shutdown stopped refined product shipments between Los Angeles and Phoenix, a pipeline official said.
The 20-inch line shut early Thursday after train cars derailed onto ground covering the segment.
"The pipeline to our knowledge is not damaged," said Jim Kehlet, director of centralized pipeline control.
He said the line, which carries 130,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of light refined petroleum products, could restart by 2300 PST Friday (0600 GMT Saturday).
The disruption will not cause shortages in Phoenix, which holds several days of supplies, he said.
He said the pipeline can move a higher volume of product to compensate for delays, but throughput will remain well below the line's 173,000 bpd capacity.
Separately, the company said workers replaced an eight-inch section of line on its San Francisco to Reno, Nevada line.
The line, which shut last weekend after a leak was suspected, carries light products to Reno at a rate of 50,000 bpd.
The line could open as early as Saturday, the company said earlier.
